items.title: SAP HANA Doesn't Have to Be a Black Box: How a Python API Can Unlock Your Data for Fiori, React
items.author: fmroque10
items.text:
A lower-complexity approach to SAP HANA reporting and dashboards 
 For : Systems Managers, CIOs, and IT Leaders working with SAP HANA. 
 If you are a Systems Manager, you know this dilemma: 
 Management asks for a quick dashboard for sales, inventory, or financial KPIs. Your data is perfect and governed within SAP HANA. But to deliver it, your team needs a senior ABAP consultant, CDS modeling, an OData service, and a Fiori developer. These are three scarce, expensive roles with a months-long learning curve. A project that should take two weeks ends up taking three months. 
 There is another way—one we are successfully implementing at several companies: a decoupled architecture. It’s not about replacing SAP; it’s about empowering it. 
 THE CORE IDEA: DECOUPLING QUERYING FROM CONSUMPTION 
 We keep SAP HANA as what it is: the best platform for transactional and analytical data. We retain SAPUI5/Fiori as the standard interface if the client desires. However, we insert a standard, open, and low-maintenance application layer in between: Python + FastAPI + REST/JSON. 
 Traditional: HANA -> CDS -> ABAP -> OData -> Fiori | 
 Decoupled: HANA -> SQL -> FastAPI -> REST/JSON -> Any Frontend [Fiori] [React] [Angular] 
 JSON becomes the universal contract. 
 TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION 
 To share with your development team 
 1. Connecting to SAP HANA Enterprise 
 We don't need the SAP development stack—just the official SAP driver. 
 pip install fastapi uvicorn hdbcli python-dotenv 
 We create a secure connection pool. We never use a "one connection per request" approach. # hana_ connector.py 
 from hdbcli import dbapi 
 import you 
 def get_hana_connection(): 
 return dbapi.connect( 
 address=os.getenv("HANA_HOST"), 
 port=int(os.getenv("HANA_PORT", "39015")), 
 user=os.getenv("HANA_USER"), 
 password=os.getenv("HANA_PASSWORD"), 
 encrypt=True # Required in prod 
 ) 
 2. The API with FastAPI - The heart of the system 
 FastAPI gives us automatic Swagger documentation, validation and asynchronous performance. Ideal for reports. 
 # main.py 
 from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException 
 from pydantic import BaseModel 
 app = FastAPI(title="SAP HANA Reporting API") 
 class SalesParams(BaseModel): 
 date_since: str 
 society: str = "1000" 
 top_n: int = 100 
 @ app.post ("/api/v1/sales/summary") 
 def get_sales_summary(params: SalesParams): 
 sql = """ 
 SELECT TOP ? "Center", SUM("NetAmount") as total 
 FROM "_SYS_BIC"."CV_SALES" 
 WHERE "AccountingDate" >= ? AND "Society" = ? 
 GROUP BY "Center" ORDER BY total DESC 
 """ 
 conn = get_hana_connection() 
 cursor = conn.cursor() 
 cursor.execute(sql, ( params.top _n, params.date _since, params.company )) 
 cols = [c[0] for c in cursor.description] 
 data = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cursor.fetchall()] 
 return {"status": "ok", "count": len(data), "data": data} 
 3. Deploy with Docker 
 FROM python:3.11-slim 
 WORKDIR /app 
 COPY requirements.txt . 
 RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt 
 COPY . . 
 CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"] 
 4. Universal Consumption: The same JSON for everyone 
 a) For Fiori / SAPUI5: 
 // SAPUI5 Controller 
 fetch("/api/v1/ventas/resumen", { 
 method: "POST", 
 body: JSON.stringify(oParams) 
 }) 
 .then(r => r.json()) 
 .then(oData => { 
 var oModel = new sap.ui.model.json.JSONModel( oData.data ); 
 this.getView().setModel(oModel, "ventas"); 
 }); 
 b) For React / Angular: 
 // React Hook with axios const { data } = useQuery(["ventas"], () => axios.post ("/api/v1/ventas/resumen", params).then(r => r.data ) ); 

 WHY SHOULD AN IT MANAGER DRIVE THIS? 
 1. Reduced Dependence on Scarce Talent: Shift from looking for "ABAP + CDS + OData + Fiori" to "SQL + Python + REST." A market 20x larger and 40% more cost-effective. 
 2. 3x Faster Delivery: A report that takes 3–4 weeks in the traditional stack can be prototyped in 2–3 days using FastAPI. 
 3. Future-Proof and Multi-channel: Today, it’s a Fiori dashboard. Tomorrow, the same API powers a React Native app, an AI model, and a Teams bot. Zero rework. 
 4. Intact Security and Governance: HANA remains the single source of truth. Read-only API, secured with JWT / Azure AD and fully audited. We do not touch the SAP core. In a single sentence for your Board of Directors: 
 We retain SAP HANA as our data platform and Fiori as our corporate UX, yet unlock the value of our data through a layer of standard APIs that any web developer can consume—thereby reducing costs, timelines, and risks. 
 #SAPHANA #ABAP #Fiori #FastAPI #Python #SAP #DigitalTransformation #CIO

items.title: Structured Address in Payment Medium Files: A Complete Guide
items.author: Sharon_
items.text:
Introduction 
 The payments industry is undergoing a significant transformation driven by the adoption of ISO 20022 and increasing regulatory requirements. One important trend is the transition from unstructured postal addresses to structured address information in payment files. To support this transition, SAP has introduced the Structured Address capability for payment medium files. 
 The feature enables payment files to contain address elements such as street name, house number, building, floor, city, postal code, district, region, and country in dedicated fields rather than free-text address lines. This improves payment processing, bank compliance, sanctions screening, and overall payment quality. 
 This blog provides an end-to-end overview of the Structured Address feature, including: 
 Business background 
 Solution overview 
 Configuration and verification 
 Business Background Traditionally, many payment medium files stored address data in a few free-format address lines: 
 While this format is human-readable, it is difficult for banks and regulatory systems to interpret consistently. 
 Structured addresses separate the information into individual attributes. In an ISO 20022 XML payment file this becomes structured tags like <StrtNm>, <BldgNb>, <PstCd>, <TwnNm>, <Ctry> — each independently addressable by the receiving system. 
 The structured address solution allows payment medium formats to use dedicated address components for all relevant parties involved in a payment transaction. It improves payment data quality, reduces payment repair and rejection rates, and enables better interpretability between banks ad payment infrastructures. 
 Solution Overview 
 Which Parties are Covered? 
 The structured address solution supports structured addresses for the major parties that can appear in a payment chain: 

 Party Type 
 Description 
 Structure 

 Creditor 
 Party to which an amount of money is due. In a credit transfer, it is usually the supplier receiving the payment. 
 FPAYHX_CRD 

 Debtor 
 Party that owes money to the creditor. In a credit transfer, it is usually the company initiating the payment. 
 FPAYHX_DBT 

 Ultimate Creditor 
 Ultimate party to which an amount of money is due. Typically used when an alternative payee is involved. In this case, the Ultimate Creditor is the supplier to whom the invoice is posted, while the Creditor is the alternative payee receiving the payment. 
 FPAYHX_UCR 

 Ultimate Debtor 
 The party on whose behalf the payment is ultimately made. In a credit transfer, this is commonly used when the sending company code differs from the paying company code. In such cases, the Debtor is the paying company code, and the Ultimate Debtor is the sending company code. 
 FPAYP_UDB (replaces deprecated FPAYHX_UDR) 

 Creditor Agent (Beneficiary Bank) 
 Bank servicing the creditor and receiving the payment on behalf of the creditor. 
 FPAYHX_CRA 

 Debtor Agent (House Bank) 
 Bank servicing the debtor and from which the payment is initiated. 
 FPAYHX_DBA 

 Intermediary Agent 1 
 First intermediary bank in the payment routing chain between debtor and creditor banks. 
 FPAYHX_AGT1 

 Intermediary Agent 2 
 Second intermediary bank in the payment routing chain. 
 FPAYHX_AGT2 

 Intermediary Agent 3 
 Third intermediary bank in the payment routing chain. 
 FPAYHX_AGT3 

 One-Time Vendor 
 A supplier that is not maintained as a regular supplier master record with its own permanent address and bank details. The supplier information is entered for a specific transaction and stored in the accounting document. Structured address data is sourced from the transaction and mapped into the payment medium at runtime. 
 FPAYH_OTV 
 Each party structure carries a consistent set of address component fields (street, house number, building, floor, PO box, room, postal code, city, township, district, region/state, region name, country) plus up to four name fields. Address number references are held separately in FPAYH_SAD. 
 Which Address Components are Included? 
 The structured address model includes fields such as: 

 Address Component Example 
 Street Main Street 
 House Number 123 
 Building Building A 
 Floor 5 
 Room 502 
 City Shanghai 
 Township Pudong 
 District Zhangjiang 
 Postal Code 200120 
 Region Shanghai 
 Country CN 
 These fields are exposed through dedicated payment structures that can be mapped into payment medium formats. 
 The International Address Version: Paying Suppliers in Their Native Script 
 For multinational organizations that pay suppliers in countries with non-Latin scripts — Chinese characters, Arabic, Cyrillic, Hangul, Kanji, Thai — a single standard address is not enough. SAP's Business Partner master data supports multiple International Address Versions , each assigned a language key (C = Chinese, A = Arabic, G = Greek, H = Hangul, K = Kanji, R = Cyrillic, T = Thai). 
 The structured address feature integrates directly with this capability. By assigning an Address Version to a payment medium format selection variant, you tell the payment run to fetch the international address of the specified version and populate the structured address fields in the payment file accordingly. 
 How the Address Version Selection Works 
 The selection variant is configured in the Create/Assign Selection Variants activity. The following is an example: 
 Selection variant DEBK2 is linked to Address Version C (Chinese). 
 When company code 1010 processes a payment using house bank DEBK2 , the system uses this variant. 
 The payment run then fetches the Version C address from the Business Partner master record and writes it into the payment medium file. 
 If no international address of the requested version exists for a party, the system falls back to the standard (basic) address . 
 Configuration & Verification 
 Structured Address 
 The following section provides a step-by-step demonstration of how to configure the structured address solution in your system. 
 Demo scenario: Create a supplier payment where Company Code 1010 acts as the debtor (payer) and Supplier 10300001 acts as the creditor (payee). The purpose of the test is to verify that the structured address maintained for the paying company is correctly populated in the debtor postal address section of the payment medium file. 
 Step 1 — Create a Format Mapping with Structured Address Fields 
 Take adding the attributes for the Debtor party as an example. Under the Dbtr node, I created a subnode PstlAdr_New and added the street name, building number, floor, room, and other address attributes. 
 Open the Map Format Data for Payments app (ID: F2685A). 
 1. In the Mapping Type filter, select PAYM ( Payment Medium Format ). 
 2. Copy Format Mapping from DE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 to /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9. 

 3. Open the format mapping /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 and start editing. 
 4. In Format Mapping Properties , click Create Node to add a new PstlAdr_New subnode under the Dbtr node. 
 5. In the Attributes section, maintain generic data for each subnode. 
 In the Source section, select Structure Field as the mapping procedure. 

 Use the value help to search for the structure field FPAYHX-STREETNM_DBT and add it. 

 6. Repeat for all fields the payment format requires. 

 7. Save the changes and release the format. 
 Step 2 — Assign the Format Mapping to a Payment Medium Format 
 The format mapping drives which structured address fields are written into the XML output of every payment run using that format. 
 In the Create Payment Medium Formats configuration activity, c opy the format from DE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 to /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9, fill the format tree /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9, and save. 

 Step 3 — Assign the Payment Medium Format to a Payment Method and Company Code 
 In the Set Up Payment Methods for Each Country/Region for Payment Transactions configuration activity, assign the /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 payment medium format to the payment method I want to use. 

 In the Set Up Payment Medium Formats per Company Code configuration activity, assign the payment medium format to the paying company code 1010. 

 Step 4 — Maintain Address in Master Data 
 In the Edit Addresses for Company Codes configuration activity, maintain the address for company code 1010. 

 Step 5 — V erification: Create a Payment and Generate Payment Files 
 Once configured and assigned, the payment medium format automatically populates structured address information during payment medium generation. 
 I now create a payment to supplier 10300001. The expected result should be that the address information for company code 1010 in the payment files is presented in a structured way. 
 In the payment media result, I can see that /ZDE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 has been used as the payment media format for the payment. 

 In the payment file, I can see that the address information of paying company code 1010 has been included in a structured way. 

 Compare this to the unstructured equivalent, where all address content is merged into two opaque AdrLine elements — the structured version gives downstream systems (correspondent banks, compliance screening, SWIFT, local clearing) precise, independently queryable fields. 
 International Address Version 
 Unlike the previous scenario, this test verifies the structured address of the supplier (creditor) . The payment medium is configured to retrieve the Chinese international address version (Version C) maintained for the supplier business partner. 
 Step 1 — Assign an Address Version to a Selection Variant 

 In the Create/Assign Selection Variants configuration activity, create the selection variant DEBK2 for the payment medium format /DE_CGI_XML_CT_V9 and house bank DEBK2. 
 By assigning an Address Version to a payment medium format selection variant, the payment medium generation process attempts to retrieve the corresponding international address version for the relevant business partner. If the requested version exists, the structured address fields in the payment file are populated with that address version; otherwise, the system falls back to the standard address. 

 2. In the Parameter Specifications dialog, set the Address Version field to the desired version code (e.g., C for Chinese ). 

 Step 2 — Maintain Business Partner Address Versions 
 International address versions are commonly maintained and used for business partners such as suppliers and customers. 
 Activate International Address Version 
 This time, I want to pay a Chinese supplier 10300002. The master data of the supplier should include an address version in Chinese. 
 In the Activate International Address Versions - Client-Specific configuration activity, ensure the C (Chinese) version is active. 

 Maintain International Address Version in Chinese 
 1. In the Maintain Business Partner app, open the business partner 10300002. 
 2. Navigate to the Address tab and click Internat. Versions . 
 3. Select the Chinese address version, and enter the address information in Chinese. 

 Step 3 — Verification: Create a Payment and Generate Payment Files 
 When the company code is 1010 & the house bank is DEBK2, the variant DEBK2 is selected. 
 When this variant is used for payment medium creation, the supplier's Chinese international address version should be retrieved and populated into the payment medium file. In the payment file generated, the address information is presented in a structured format using the Chinese address version. 

 Summary The Structured Address solution replaces traditional free-text address lines with dedicated address components. Through configurable format mappings, support for all major payment parties, and integration with business partner international address versions, organizations can generate payment files that are more compliant, more accurate, and better aligned with ISO 20022 requirements. All the available structures and fields are available in the SAP Help Portal: Maintaining Format Mappings for Structured Addresses | SAP H

items.title: MEK3 condition type for plant specific is maintained but not reflecting in PO
items.author: Rincie
items.text:
Issue Description 
 The PO net price determination is working correctly in QAS when either one of the applicable MEK1 condition key combinations is maintained. However, in PRD, when only one key combination is maintained, the PO sometimes does not fetch the correct updated price and may consider the previous PO price. 
 QAS Scenario 
 For the material, MEK1 condition key combination 017 (Material Info Record – Plant Specific) is maintained with a price of 4.70, while key combination 018 is not maintained. 
 When the PO is created, the system correctly fetches the price of 4.70 from the maintained condition record. 
 Hence, in QAS, if any one applicable key combination is maintained, the PO is fetching the correct maintained price. 
 QAS Screenshot 1 – MEK1 Condition Record (017) 

 QAS Screenshot 2 – PO Showing Correct Price 4.70 

 PRD Scenario – Only 017 Maintained 
 The same condition setup is maintained in PRD: key combination 017 is maintained with a price of 4.70, while key combination 018 is not maintained. 
 However, while creating the PO, the net price is sometimes not fetched correctly as per the updated condition. In some cases, the system is considering the previous PO price of 4.50. 
 PRD Screenshot 1 – MEK1 Condition Record (017) 

 PRD Screenshot 2 – PO Showing Price 4.50 

 PRD Screenshot 3 – PO is taking previous PO before updating the new price. 

 PRD Validation – Both 017 and 018 Maintained 
 As a validation, condition key combination 018 was also maintained for the same material with a price of 4.70. After both 017 and 018 were maintained, the PO correctly fetched the price of 4.70. 
 This indicates that the issue occurs in PRD when only one applicable key combination is maintained. 
 PRD Screenshot 4 – Both 017 & 018 Maintained / PO Fetching 4.70 

 Validation – Different Price Maintained for 018 
 When the 018 condition was maintained with a price of 4.80, the PO in PRD considered the 018 price of 4.80 instead of the plant-specific price of 4.70. However, the same scenario is working correctly in QAS, where the plant-specific price of 4.70 is considered. 
 Expected Behavior 
 If either one of the applicable MEK1 key combinations (017 or 018) is maintained with a valid condition price, the PO should fetch the corresponding correct price. The system should not consider the previous PO price when a valid condition record is available. 
 QAS & PRD Version Details 
 QAS SAP / System Version: S4hana 1609 
 PRD SAP / System Version: S4hana 2025 
 Request to SAP 
 Kindly check the above behavior and identify the root cause for the difference between QAS and PRD. Please verify the relevant pricing/condition determination and system configuration and advise why the PO is fetching the correct price in QAS with either one key combination, whereas in PRD the correct price is fetched only when both key combinations are maintained.

items.title: Se excede tope de seguridad social en adelanto de vacaciones
items.author: FacundoQuevedo
items.text:
El caso es el siguiente: 
 La empleada tiene 14 días de vacaciones : 9 en septiembre y 5 en octubre. 
 El adelanto de vacaciones se paga en septiembre por los 14 días completos . 
 Por esos 14 días, el tope proporcional es $2.189.482,62 . 
 Luego, en la liquidación de septiembre, quedan 16 días para completar el mes (30 - 14). 
 Por esos 16 días, el tope que corresponde aplicar es $2.502.265,85 . 
 Entonces: 
 $2.189.482,62 + $2.502.265,85 = $4.691.748,47 
 Esto coincide exactamente con el tope legal mensual de septiembre , por lo que es correcto. 
 El problema aparece si en septiembre se toman los 21 días de la liquidación para calcular el tope: 
 $2.189.482,62 + $3.284.223,67 = $5.473.706,29 
 Eso supera el tope legal mensual , por lo que es incorrecto. 

 Entiendo que el igualmente se ajusta una parte en octubre por eso 5 dias, pero entiendo que es incorrecto que supere el tope en septiembre. 

 Como podria solucionarlo ?

items.author: nimmala_prasanthkumar44a1ef
items.text:
Hi all, 
 We use batch determination based on a Customer-Material freshness requirement. If freshness is maintained as 70%, only batches with freshness ≥70% should be selected during delivery creation. 
 Stock: 
 Batch 1: 75% freshness, Qty 2 
 Batch 2: 50% freshness, Qty 5 
 Batch 3: 60% freshness, Qty 5 
 A sales order is created for Qty 4. 
 Case 1 
 Delivery is created with proposed Qty 4. 
 Batch determination finds only Qty 2 from Batch 1 (eligible batch). 
 After saving, delivery quantity is automatically reduced to Qty 2. 
 Sales order header shows "Partially Delivered". 
 However, table (VBUK) level status is updated as "Delivery Completed". 
 Later, new stock arrives: 
 Batch 4: 80% freshness, Qty 5 
 When creating the next delivery, the system issues: "No delivery-relevant items in order xxx" 
 The remaining Qty 2 is not considered for delivery, although eligible stock exists. 
 Case 2 
 If delivery quantity is manually changed from Qty 4 to Qty 2 before saving the first delivery, item status remains "Partially Delivered". 
 A second delivery can then be created successfully using Batch 4. 
 Question: Why is the Table (VBUK) level being marked as "Delivery Completed" in Case 1 when only Qty 2 of Qty 4 is delivered? Which status/update logic controls this behavior, and how can it be corrected so that subsequent deliveries can be created when eligible stock becomes available later? 

 Thanks, 
 Nimmala Prasanthkumar.

digest.headline: Thin day for ABAP: one solid RAP change-log tutorial, an email-template post, and mostly forum questions plus Joule Studio coverage.
digest.overview:
The one substantial technical item is a guide to RAP change logging on the BTP ABAP Environment. It uses the standard Change Document Object, the `changedocuments` directive in the behavior definition, and a custom entity with a query provider to show history [5]. A second useful post covers branded HTML email in S/4HANA with email templates, `CL_SMTG_EMAIL_API`, `CL_BCS` and CID inline images [63]. A RAP hierarchical business object post was collected, but only its abstract was available, so it has no usable content [7].

The rest is forum questions with little or no answer: F4 help filtered by BUKRS [47], My Inbox BADI selection [21], routing validation BADIs [40], a PNP selection screen gap [45], and several integration and provisioning errors [26, 86, 92, 101]. There are also two Joule Studio items, one overview and one webinar advert [57, 84]. For training, the change-log post is the one to teach from. The questions show recurring gaps in extension-point discovery and in dependent F4 help design.

top_stories.summary: The post sets up a Change Document Object in ADT and enables the Change Document Logging flag on each data element, which is easy to miss. It then adds `changedocuments` to the behavior definition (create: key, update: data, delete: none). History is exposed through a RAP custom entity with `@ObjectModel.query.implementedBy`. The query provider implements `if_rap_query_provider~select`, reads changes with `cl_chdo_read_tools=>changedocument_read()`, and handles filters via `io_request->get_filter()->get_as_ranges()`. Fields mapped include changenr, tabkey, fname, old/new values, chngind (I/U/D), udate, utime and username.

deep_dives.title: RAP change documents: behavior definition plus custom entity history
deep_dives.explanation:
The standard route avoids a hand-built audit table. First create a Change Document Object in ADT. Then enable the Change Document Logging flag on every data element whose field you want tracked. This is the step most likely to be missed, and without it nothing is written.

In the behavior definition, the `changedocuments` directive names the object and the logging mode per operation. The post uses create: key, update: data, delete: none, so RAP writes the change documents as part of the save sequence.

To display history, define a RAP custom entity annotated with `@ObjectModel.query.implementedBy: 'ABAP:...'`. The class implements `if_rap_query_provider~select`. It converts the request filter with `io_request->get_filter()->get_as_ranges()`, calls `cl_chdo_read_tools=>changedocument_read()`, and maps the result fields: changenr, tabkey, fname, value_shstr_old, value_shstr_new, chngind, udate, utime and username. Because the provider builds the result in ABAP, you must also handle paging and sorting yourself if the UI sends them.

deep_dives.title: Template-driven HTML email with CL_SMTG_EMAIL_API and CL_BCS
deep_dives.explanation:
The design separates content from logic. Subject and body are stored as Email Templates in S/4HANA, and ABAP only supplies data and sends. `CL_SMTG_EMAIL_API` handles the template side, with `CL_BCS` as the underlying send infrastructure.

Inline images use CID references (RFC 2392 Content-ID). The HTML refers to the image as `cid:...` and the image part is attached with a matching Content-ID. This lets signatures and logos render in the body instead of appearing as separate attachments.

The trade-off to teach is template governance versus code control. Content changes then follow the template maintenance process rather than a code transport.

deep_dives.title: Dependent F4 help: why BSIS and SKA1 both fail the BUKRS requirement
deep_dives.explanation:
The question tries two table-based search help references. BSIS-HKONT is a large line-item table, so the F4 is slow. SKA1-SAKNR is chart-of-accounts level and has no BUKRS, so it cannot filter by company code [47].

The material gives no accepted answer, so what follows is a general approach. The account-to-company-code assignment sits in SKB1, which carries both BUKRS and SAKNR. A search help or value help based on SKB1 can use BUKRS as an input parameter, and a search help exit can read the screen value of BUKRS. This is a design suggestion, not something stated in the source.

The lesson is to pick the table that holds the filter key and to avoid line-item tables for master-data lookups.

interview_questions.question: How would you implement change history for a RAP business object without a custom audit table, and how would you display it?
interview_questions.answer: Use the standard Change Document framework. Create a Change Document Object in ADT and enable the Change Document Logging flag on each data element you want tracked. Without that flag nothing is logged. Then add the `changedocuments` directive to the behavior definition, specifying logging per operation, for example create: key, update: data, delete: none. To display history, build a RAP custom entity with `@ObjectModel.query.implementedBy`. The query class implements `if_rap_query_provider~select`, converts the filter with `get_as_ranges()`, and reads the data with `cl_chdo_read_tools=>changedocument_read()`. It maps the fields (changenr, tabkey, fname, old and new values, chngind, date, time, user) to the entity. Paging and sorting have to be handled in the provider.

interview_questions.question: Why use email templates with CL_SMTG_EMAIL_API instead of building HTML in ABAP, and how do inline images work?
interview_questions.answer: Templates keep subject and body outside the code, so branding or wording changes do not need a code transport and can follow template governance. ABAP supplies only the data and triggers the send. `CL_SMTG_EMAIL_API` works with the templates, and `CL_BCS` provides the underlying send infrastructure. For inline images, the HTML references the image with a `cid:` Content-ID (RFC 2392). The image is added as a related part with the same Content-ID, so it renders in the body instead of appearing as an attachment. The trade-off is that you lose some programmatic control over the HTML structure.

interview_questions.question: A BADI implementation for a standard Fiori app extension never triggers. How do you diagnose it?
interview_questions.answer: First confirm you chose the right enhancement spot, because similar BADIs exist, as in the My Inbox case with `/IWWRK/ES_TGW_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE` and `/IWPGW/BADI_TGW_TASK_DATA` [21]. Check that the implementation is active, any filter values match, and the BADI is called for your scenario. Set a breakpoint in the BADI call point or in `CL_EXITHANDLER`. Then verify the app-side configuration, such as the catalog tile parameter `showAdditionalAttributes`, so the request actually reaches that code path. If the app is task-type specific, check that your task is registered for that scenario. Finally, check the gateway service and trace the backend call to see which BADI is hit.
